AttentionItem.description: One ledger row. `title` and `body` are written by core so every client says the same thing; a client that knows the chat may render its own.

approvalEventId.description: For `needsYou`: the session-forest sequence of the request, which is what `approvals/resolve_approval` takes as its event id.

resolvedAt.description: Set when the request was answered, by the person or by policy.

sequence.description: The ledger cursor. Strictly increasing, never reused.

oneOf.description: A top-level chat finished a turn.

A visible chat, workers included, is waiting on the person.
Input queued for a chat whose adapter is gone has waited past the bound. `sessions/deliver_queued_input` delivers it.
An agent asked for the person (`attention/post`, the `notify_user` tool). Title and body are the agent's own words.

A kind added after this client was built. The ledger gains kinds slice by slice; decoding them as `other` keeps an older client's read working instead of failing it, and a client shows nothing for them.
A severity added after this client was built.
A turn ended with an error.
The chat waits on the person: an approval, a permission or a question.
No turn is in flight and nothing waits on the person.
